title: eCounter: Inline Per-IP Network Monitoring at Millisecond Resolution via eBPF
problem: Scientific data acquisition needs sub-millisecond network telemetry; existing tools lack fine-grained observability
motivation: Streaming SciDAQ requires real-time monitoring; P4 switches expensive; host-side tools insufficient
method: The system embeds monitoring code directly into the Linux kernel using eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter), a framework that lets programs run in kernel space with minimal overhead. It categorizes incoming network packets by IP address and protocol type (TCP, UDP, etc.) and records traffic counts at millisecond-scale resolution. Because the monitoring runs at kernel level rather than as a separate application, it captures detailed per-IP network behavior with very little CPU consumption—crucial for scientific experiments that need accurate, real-time network performance data.
key_novelty: By running network monitoring directly in the Linux kernel via eBPF, the system achieves per-IP telemetry at sub-millisecond resolution with only 4% CPU overhead and no need for special hardware.
